# Part II — Hardware and wiring

The jaytek_v1 board and everything that connects to it: tools, wiring practice, power and grounds, sensors, outputs, CAN and the rest of the vehicle. Read it before you build or check a harness.

- **[7 The jaytek_v1 board](07-board.md)** — The jaytek_v1 is the ECU hardware — three sealed harness connectors, the input and output circuits behind them, and a USB link to the studio — and this chapter is its map.
- **[8 Tools and materials](08-tools.md)** — The tools and materials you need to build a harness for the jaytek_v1 board, test it, and bench-test the ECU before it goes near an engine.
- **[9 Wiring practice](09-wiring-practice.md)** — How to build a harness for the jaytek_v1 board that carries clean signals, survives heat, water and vibration, and can be understood and repaired years later.
- **[10 Power, grounds and protection](10-power-grounds.md)** — How the ECU is powered, how it decides the key is on, where its grounds go, what protects it, and how to wire all of that so every sensor reading and every injector pulse can be trusted.
- **[11 Wiring sensors](11-wiring-sensors.md)** — How to connect every kind of sensor to the ECU — which pin type it wants, where its power and ground come from, and how to keep its signal clean.
- **[12 Wiring outputs](12-wiring-outputs.md)** — How to connect injectors, coils, relays, PWM valves, motors and stepper valves to the ECU's outputs, what each kind of output can and cannot drive, and how to prove each one works before the engine runs.
- **[13 CAN bus](13-can-bus.md)** — CAN is a two-wire network that lets the ECU talk to dashes, wideband controllers, I/O boxes and scan tools; this chapter is about wiring it so it works.
- **[14 Vehicle integration](14-vehicle-integration.md)** — How to connect the ECU to the rest of the car — fuel pump, cooling fans, air conditioning, tachometer, dash, road speed and the diagnostic port.
